newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker after Thiessen testimony.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker after Thiessen testimony.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday, with spreads to U.S. bonds widening, as the Canadian dollar slipped after testimony by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen.

"It left open the possibility that the Bank would not respond to a Fed tightening move initially, so then there's concern about the currency and the currency sold off," said Sherry Cooper, chief economist at Nesbitt Burns.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.45 to C$108.83 to yield 7.242 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
The Canadian 30-year bond is now trading at its lowest point since January. The spread between the two widened to 28 basis points from 25 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

Canada's dollar was weaker this afternoon and spreads to U.S. Treasuries widened after Thiessen told the Senate Banking Committee that Canada's improved finances had given the central bank more room for maneuver in response to possible U.S. interest rate rise.
Canadian bonds had already opened weaker on concern strong U.S. data released this morning makes a rate hike more likely.
Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets weaked after the U.S. Commerce Department reported that housing starts in February reached their highest levels in almost three years.
Cooper said if the Bank of Canada did not initially match a Fed hike and the currency weakened, it could force the bank to hike rates, which would be a major negative for Canadian bonds.

Analysts said both Canadian and U.S. bond investors are now focused on the U.S. consumer price index report for February out tomorrow. The report is expected to provide further clues about the possibility of a Fed rate hike.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.35 to C$102.75 yielding 6.609 percent while the U.S. 10-year traded unchanged to yield 6.72 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 11 basis points from 16 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.13 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.28 percent.
